sanskrit_verse:
तस्माद् देशे च काले च वणिगर्घं पराक्रमेत् ।
न जिह्मेण प्रवर्तेत श्रेयानेवं वणिक्पथः ॥
transliteration: tasmād deśe ca kāle ca vaṇig-arhaṃ parākramet | na jihmeṇa pravarteta śreyān evaṃ vaṇik-pathaḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Therefore, a merchant shall act according to the value of place and time; he should not engage in crooked conduct. Such is the superior path of commerce.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from alignment with Dharma, not personal desire.
Causation arises through right action attuned to context.
Restoration logic demands that economic activity align with cosmic order.
Consciousness alignment ensures transactions elevate both parties.
executable_legal_axioms: IF merchant acts without regard to deśa-kāla-yoga THEN transaction invalidates until realignment occurs.
IF intent involves jihma (deceit) THEN system flags for integrity reintegration protocol.
IF transaction upholds śreya (higher good) THEN it auto-aligns with dharmic ledger.
IF vaṇik-patha deviation detected THEN initiate consciousness recalibration sequence.
supreme_court_application: In commercial disputes, the Supreme Court must assess whether the actor demonstrated deśa-kāla-yoga awareness. Intentions lacking transparency invoke automatic referral to Nyāya-based restoration mechanisms rather than punitive measures.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that all actions arise from causal alignment. Jihma disrupts this flow. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how deceit leads to systemic dissonance. Proportional responsibility lies in restoring clarity, not inflicting consequence. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that misaligned action dissolves when consciousness returns to śreya.
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Dharma governs commerce through consciousness. No punishment arises—only restoration. The path of the merchant is purified by alignment. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates truth.
